# Cold Dark Matter with Baryonic Feedback (ΛCDM) as an Explanation of the Cosmic-Shear / S₈ Amplitude Tension

## 1. Concept Synthesis

Cold Dark Matter with baryonic feedback — the ΛCDM paradigm augmented with realistic astrophysical galaxy formation physics — remains the mainstream explanation for the observed **S₈ amplitude tension**: the systematic deficit of large-scale-structure growth inferred from weak-lensing surveys relative to CMB-inferred ΛCDM predictions.

**The observable.** Cosmic shear surveys measure the lensing distortion of background galaxy shapes by intervening matter. Under ΛCDM the amplitude of this signal is governed by σ₈ (rms matter fluctuations in 8 h⁻¹Mpc spheres) and the matter density Ω_m, conventionally combined as S₈ ≡ σ₈(Ω_m/0.3)^0.5 [GENERAL]. Planck CMB temperature/polarization data, when extrapolated via ΛCDM to z ≈ 0, give S₈ = 0.832 ± 0.013 [VERIFIED: Planck 2018 VI, DOI 10.1051/0004-6361/201833910]. Direct weak-lensing surveys find consistently lower values: KiDS-1000 gives S₈ = 0.759 (+0.024/−0.021) [VERIFIED: Asgari et al. 2021, DOI 10.1051/0004-6361/202039070], a 2.85σ tension (ΔS₈ = −0.073 ± 0.026; independent Gaussian recomputation: 2.81σ, Δχ² = 7.9), and DES-Y3 gives S₈ = 0.776 ± 0.017 [VERIFIED: Amon et al. 2022, DOI 10.1103/PhysRevD.105.023520], a 2.62σ tension (recomputed 2.62σ, Δχ² = 6.85). This pattern — a low LSS amplitude relative to the same ΛCDM model that fits the CMB — is the central anomaly.

**The ΛCDM + baryonic feedback explanation.** Within ΛCDM, the cold dark matter skeleton of structure formation is untouched; the discrepancy is attributed to the *baryonic* component. AGN jets, supernova winds, and stellar feedback eject gas from potential wells, redistributing mass on scales k ≈ 0.1–10 h/Mpc. Because gas is gravitationally coupled to dark matter, the *total* matter power spectrum is suppressed at small scales relative to a baryon-free DMB (dark-matter-only) calculation. Since cosmic shear integrates the nonlinear matter power spectrum along the line of sight, unmodeled baryonic suppression biases the inferred S₈ downward — i.e., lensing surveys that assume dark-matter-only power recover artificially low S₈ even if the true cosmology matches Planck. Amon & Efstathiou [VERIFIED, DOI 10.1093/mnras/stac2429] demonstrated that a simple parameterized nonlinear suppression of the matter power spectrum can reconcile KiDS-1000, DES-Y3, HSC, and Planck S₈ values, effectively dissolving the tension as a modeling (not cosmological) effect. The FLAMINGO suite of cosmological hydrodynamical simulations [VERIFIED: Schaye et al. 2023, DOI 10.1093/mnras/stad2419] — with AGN/stellar feedback calibrated to the observed galaxy stellar mass function and cluster gas fractions — shows the required suppression is broadly achievable, though the strength of feedback required is at the *high* end of what galaxy observations tolerate.

**Status assessment.** The S₈ tension itself is [VERIFIED] as a persistent inter-survey discrepancy (2–3σ, present in KiDS-450 onward [VERIFIED: Hildebrandt et al. 2016, DOI 10.1093/mnras/stw2805], KiDS-1000, DES-Y3, HSC-Y3 [VERIFIED: Dalal et al. 2023, DOI 10.1103/physrevd.108.123519]). The *baryonic-feedback resolution* is [THEORETICAL]/model-dependent: it requires (i) feedback stronger than in many standard simulations (e.g., original BAHAMAS-calibrated runs), (ii) a suppression shape (sharp drop near k ≈ 9 h/Mpc then partial recovery) that FLAMINGO variants can only partially reproduce, and (iii) consistency with kSZ/X-ray cluster gas constraints, which currently favor *weaker* feedback than the S₈-reconciliation prescription [MODEL-DEPENDENT: AGN feedback strength calibrated to gas fractions vs. stellar mass function].

- S₈ tension existence: **[VERIFIED]** (multiple independent surveys, consistent 2–3σ deficit).
- Baryonic-feedback magnitude within ΛCDM: **[VERIFIED]** qualitatively (hydrodynamical simulations universally find suppression at k ≳ 1 h/Mpc).
- Baryonic feedback *as full resolution of the S₈ tension*: **[THEORETICAL]** — requires feedback at the aggressive end of calibrations and remains in tension with kSZ/X-ray gas constraints; not yet adjudicated.
- H₀ tension: **[VERIFIED]** at ~5σ; baryonic feedback does *not* address it (it is an LSS-amplitude problem), illustrating that S₈ and H₀ tensions may have distinct origins — a point emphasized in the CosmoVerse literature.

**Limitations**: (i) baryonic suppression modeling is degenerate with intrinsic alignments and photo-z systematics in shear surveys; (ii) simulation calibration targets (stellar mass function vs. gas fractions) are mutually inconsistent at current precision; (iii) Gaussian tension estimates understate non-Gaussian, parameter-correlated tension structure; (iv) Stage-IV analyses using large scales only will bypass baryonic physics and definitively test the hypothesis.

# Decaying Dark Matter into Dark Radiation as a Solution to the S₈ Cosmic-Shear Tension: A Critical Synthesis

---

## 1. Executive Summary

The S₈ tension — a persistent discrepancy between the amplitude of matter fluctuations inferred from the cosmic microwave background (CMB, assuming ΛCDM) and that measured directly by late-universe weak gravitational lensing surveys — is one of the most robust anomalies in modern cosmology. Combined analyses constrain the parameter S₈ ≡ σ₈(Ω_m/0.3)^0.5: Planck 2018 finds S₈ = 0.832 ± 0.013 [12], while KiDS-1000 finds S₈ = 0.759⁺⁰·²⁴₋₀.₀₂₁ [13] and DES-Y3 finds S₈ = 0.776 ± 0.017 [14], corresponding to Gaussian tensions of ≈2.85σ (Δχ² = 7.9) and ≈2.62σ (Δχ² = 6.85) respectively.

One class of particle-physics-motivated resolution is **decaying dark matter (DDM)**: a cold dark matter particle χ of mass m_χ that decays with lifetime τ_χ = Γ⁻¹ of order the Hubble time into an invisible, effectively massless species — dark radiation (DR), possibly itself interacting with the residual DM. Because ρ_χ decays as a⁻³e^(−Γt), the *fraction* of non-relativistic matter decreases over cosmic time, the effective CDM growth rate is suppressed at late epochs, and σ₈ (and hence S₈) is reduced relative to Planck-normalized ΛCDM — exactly in the direction required by the data. Dedicated analyses [1, 2, 3] confirm that late-decaying DM (τ_χ ≳ a few Gyr) with decay products in the warm/DR sector can soften or statistically absorb the S₈ tension, while remaining consistent with CMB, BAO, and Lyman-α constraints.

However, the literature is divided. McCarthy & Hill [6] argue that converting DM to DR **does not** fully resolve the combined cosmological-tension landscape when joint CMB + BAO + lensing + supernova analyses are performed. Anchordoqui et al. [5] show that decays occurring before recombination to DR are severely constrained by CMB polarization data, so only late decays help S₈ — but late decays do nothing for H₀. This report presents the mathematical framework, the empirical status, the model's validity domain, the skeptical counter-evidence, competing alternative hypotheses (baryonic feedback, early dark energy, interacting dark sectors, modified gravity), and a synthesis of what current data permit.

**Bottom line:** DDM→DR is a *viable but partial and model-dependent* S₈ resolution: it robustly suppresses late-time growth and can reconcile Planck with weak-lensing amplitudes at ~2σ significance, but it fails to simultaneously address the H₀ and DESI dark-energy tensions, and its parameter space is tightly squeezed by Lyman-α, CMB anisotropies, and ΔN_eff bounds.

## 2. Observational Landscape: Where Textbook ΛCDM Meets the Data

### 2.1 The S₈ tension quantified

- **Planck 2018 TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing** [12]: S₈ = 0.832 ± 0.013; σ₈(Ω_m)⁰·⁵ normalization with σ₈ = 0.8111 ± 0.0060.
- **KiDS-1000 cosmic shear** [13]: S₈ = 0.759⁺⁰·²⁴₋₀.₀₂₁, tension 2.85σ vs Planck (Δχ² = 7.9 between ΛCDM fits).
- **DES-Y3** (3×2pt) [14]: S₈ = 0.776 ± 0.017, tension 2.62σ (Δχ² = 6.85).
- Extensions such as KiDS-1000 + external data reduce but do not eliminate the preference for growth suppression [25]. Stage-IV forecasting shows that the tension will become decisive (>5σ equivalent) unless systematic uncertainties in nonlinear modeling are resolved [26].
- **Cluster count corroboration**: DES-Y1 cluster abundances [27] independently prefer lower σ₈ than Planck, and X-ray mass calibration systematics [28] remain a known caveat at the ~few-percent level.

### 2.2 Adjacent tensions that constrain any DDM model

- **H₀**: Planck 67.36 ± 0.54 km/s/Mpc vs SH0ES 73.04 ± 1.04 → ~4.85σ [15, 16, 17]. JWST has confirmed the SH0ES Cepheid photometry at 8σ confidence against crowding systematics [16].
- **DESI dynamical dark energy**: DESI DR2 BAO (with CMB/SNe) prefers evolving w₀wₐCDM at 2.5–3.9σ depending on the supernova sample [20].
- **Inflationary**: BICEP/Keck bound r₀.₀₅ < 0.036 (95%) [18]; NANOGrav 15-yr detects a common stochastic process at f = 1 yr⁻¹ with amplitude A_GWB = 2.4⁺⁰·⁷₋₀.₆×10⁻¹⁵ [19].
- **Gravity**: GW170817 limits |c_gw − c|/c ≲ 10⁻¹⁵, ruling out most simple scalar-tensor screening modifications of gravity in the strong-coupling regime.

These adjacent tensions matter because, as shown below, DDM→DR helps S₈ through late-time physics but leaves the pre-recombination sound horizon (and hence H₀) essentially untouched.

### 3.2 Validity Domain & Claim Scope

**[GENERAL]** claims (robust across all analyses):
1. In any scenario where DM converts to relativistic energy at late times, ρ_dm(a) declines faster than a⁻³, the combination G_eff(a)·ρ_m(a) driving gravitational growth decreases, and σ₈/S₈ is suppressed relative to a fixed-CMB ΛCDM fit. This is a kinematic consequence of the Boltzmann and growth equations and holds regardless of microphysical details of the decay product.
2. CMB primary anisotropies are largely insensitive to *late* (z ≲ 10–100) energy release, because the relevant modes' transfer functions freeze after horizon entry; hence late decays are far less constrained than pre-recombination ones — the latter are strongly bounded by CMB temperature/polarization damping tails and by ΔN_eff [5].

**[MODEL-DEPENDENT]** claims:
1. The *magnitude* of achievable S₈ suppression depends on the decay product's velocity distribution: decay products carrying nonzero peculiar velocities induce free-streaming cut-off scales in P_δ ("warm decay products"), so the allowed parameter volume (Γ⁻¹, m_χ, v_decay) is set by Lyman-α forest 1D flux power [3]. Purely lightlike DR decay products maximize S₈ suppression at fixed observational cost; warm products are more constrained.
2. Whether DDM→DR constitutes a statistically acceptable *resolution* of S₈ (as opposed to a mere improvement in fit) is analysis-dependent: profile-likelihood treatments show that Bayesian MCMC posteriors in decaying-DM parameter space can be contaminated by volume effects in the extremes of τ_χ [9].
3. Any claim that DDM also fixes H₀ requires pre-recombination decays, which CMB polarization disfavors at high significance [5]; post-recombination decay modifying only late growth cannot move the sound horizon [6].

# Stable Cold Dark Matter with Baryonic Feedback vs Decaying Dark Matter in Resolving the S₈ Tension

## 1. Overview
The cosmic-shear **S₈ tension** is a persistent 2–3σ discrepancy between the lower amplitude of late-time structure inferred from weak-lensing surveys and the higher amplitude predicted by extrapolating Planck CMB observations within ΛCDM. The leading conventional explanation is ΛCDM with baryonic feedback: energetic processes in galaxies and clusters redistribute gas and suppress nonlinear matter clustering. Decaying dark matter into dark radiation (DDM→DR) is a legitimate, but weaker, alternative that changes the growth of structure.

**Comparative verdict:** ΛCDM with baryonic feedback is the leading conventional explanation; DDM→DR remains a theoretical alternative with substantial observational constraints and no direct detection of dark-matter decay. Neither explanation addresses the H₀ tension.

**Skeptic score:** 5/5.
**Math status:** [MATH_CONSISTENT], 3.5/4. Two equations—the tension formula and σ₈ integral—were manually checked rather than tool-verified. The dimensional error in the growth equation identified in the review must be corrected as shown below.

## 2. Detailed Explanation
### The observational discrepancy

Cosmic shear measures the distortion of background galaxy images by intervening matter. Its amplitude is often summarized by

\[
S_8 \equiv \sigma_8\left(\frac{\Omega_m}{0.3}\right)^{0.5},
\]

where \(\sigma_8\) is the present-day rms linear matter fluctuation in spheres of radius \(8\,h^{-1}\mathrm{Mpc}\), and \(\Omega_m\) is the present matter density parameter.

The verified values are:

| Data set | \(S_8\) |
|---|---:|
| Planck | \(0.832\pm0.013\) |
| KiDS-1000, shear-only | \(0.759^{+0.024}_{-0.021}\) |
| DES-Y3 | \(0.776\pm0.017\) |

Using the stated independent Gaussian uncertainties, the recomputed Planck comparisons are **2.81σ for KiDS-1000** and **2.62σ for DES-Y3**. These results support the characterization of the S₈ discrepancy as a persistent, inter-survey 2–3σ tension.

The KiDS-1000 attribution needs care: the value \(S_8=0.759\) is the shear-only result associated with Asgari et al. The DOI 10.1051/0004-6361/202039070 is identified in the approved review as Heymans et al.’s 3x2pt result, with \(S_8\approx0.766\), and should not be used to cite the shear-only value.

### Leading conventional explanation: baryonic feedback

AGN activity, stellar feedback, and supernova-driven outflows can displace gas from gravitational potential wells. Because baryons and dark matter are gravitationally coupled, this redistribution suppresses the total nonlinear matter power spectrum relative to a dark-matter-only calculation, particularly at \(k\gtrsim1\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}\). Hydrodynamical simulations qualitatively verify this suppression.

Cosmic shear integrates the projected matter power spectrum. If baryonic suppression is inadequately modeled, lensing analyses can infer a lower \(S_8\) than would be obtained with a correct model. Thus baryonic feedback could reduce the apparent discrepancy without changing the underlying cold-dark-matter framework.

However, **feedback as a full resolution remains theoretical and contested**. The required strength is at the high end of calibrations and conflicts with kSZ and X-ray constraints on gas fractions. The size of that feedback-versus-kSZ tension still needs to be quantified in \(\Delta\chi^2\).

### Alternative: decaying dark matter into dark radiation

In DDM→DR models, some dark matter decays into relativistic dark radiation. The resulting change in the matter content and growth history can suppress late-time structure formation, potentially lowering the predicted \(S_8\).

This mechanism is theoretical, not directly detected. It is squeezed by Lyman-α constraints and limits on additional relativistic energy density, including Planck’s \(N_{\mathrm{eff}}=2.99\pm0.17\). McCarthy & Hill (2023) find only marginal gains in joint fits. DDM→DR also does **not** address H₀: pre-recombination decays are excluded by CMB polarization constraints (Anchordoqui et al. 2022).

### Distinguishing the explanations

The mechanisms predict different scale and time dependence:

- **Baryonic feedback:** primarily suppresses small, nonlinear scales.
- **DDM→DR:** changes growth across scales, with a late-time, redshift-dependent signature.

Stage-IV weak-lensing tomography from Euclid and LSST, together with measurements of \(f\sigma_8(z)\), can help distinguish these patterns.

## 3. Mathematical Framework
### Definitions and corrected equations

The Gaussian tension estimate for independent measurements is

\[
N_\sigma=\frac{|\Delta|}{\sqrt{\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2}},
\qquad
\Delta\chi^2=N_\sigma^2.
\]

With correlated uncertainties, the denominator generalizes to \(\sqrt{\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2-2\rho\sigma_1\sigma_2}\).

The standard linear growth equation for matter perturbations in ΛCDM is

\[
\ddot{\delta}+2H\dot{\delta}
-\frac{3}{2}\Omega_m H_0^2a^{-3}\delta=0.
\]

The \(H_0^2/M_{\rm Pl}^2\) factor appearing in both reports’ growth equation is dimensionally inconsistent in that form. The correct source term contains \(H_0^2\), with **no \(M_{\rm Pl}^{-2}\)**. The same correction applies to the DDM drag-term coefficients.

The variance defining \(\sigma_8\) can be written as

\[
\sigma_8^2=\int_0^\infty \frac{dk}{k}\,
\frac{k^3P_{\rm lin}(k)}{2\pi^2}
\left|W(kR_8)\right|^2,
\]

where \(R_8=8\,h^{-1}\mathrm{Mpc}\), and

\[
W(x)=3\,\frac{\sin x-x\cos x}{x^3}.
\]

This integral was manually verified; it was not tool-verified.

### Baryonic modification to the power spectrum

A useful schematic relation is

\[
P_\delta(k,z)=B(k,z)P_{\rm DMO}(k,z),
\]

where \(P_{\rm DMO}\) denotes the dark-matter-only power spectrum and \(B(k,z)\) is a baryonic modification. The Amon–Efstathiou \(B(k)\) ansatz is phenomenological, has about six free parameters, and can be degenerate with intrinsic alignments and photometric-redshift systematics. Fitting it to the same shear data it is intended to reconcile carries a circularity risk.

### DDM growth modification

A schematic DDM growth equation includes a drag contribution from the interaction with dark radiation. Its coefficients must use dimensionally consistent physical units; the erroneous \(M_{\rm Pl}^{-2}\) factor must not be retained. The detailed DDM claims also require profile-likelihood treatment, as emphasized by Brinch Holm et al.

### Tension benchmarks

| Comparison | Recomputed tension |
|---|---:|
| Planck–KiDS-1000 \(S_8\) | 2.81σ |
| Planck–DES-Y3 \(S_8\) | 2.62σ |
| Planck–SH0ES \(H_0\) | 4.85σ |

The \(H_0\) discrepancy is separate from the S₈ comparison. Neither baryonic feedback nor DDM→DR resolves the 4.85σ H₀ tension.

## 4. Skeptical Perspectives & Alternative Hypotheses
- **Feedback may not be strong enough.** Reconciliation requires feedback near the high end of calibrations and is in tension with kSZ/X-ray gas-fraction constraints. This disagreement should be quantified using \(\Delta\chi^2\).
- **The feedback model is not uniquely identified by shear.** Flexible suppression models can be degenerate with intrinsic alignments and photometric-redshift systematics. The Amon–Efstathiou \(B(k)\) model’s several free parameters also make same-data fitting vulnerable to circularity.
- **DDM→DR is constrained and indirect.** Lyman-α and \(\Delta N_{\rm eff}\) limit the available parameter space; there is no direct detection of dark-matter decay. Joint-fit improvements reported by McCarthy & Hill (2023) are marginal.
- **DDM claims need stronger statistical treatment.** Profile likelihoods, including the approach highlighted by Brinch Holm et al., should be used rather than relying solely on parameter posterior summaries.
- **The scale and redshift signatures offer a test.** Feedback acts chiefly on nonlinear small scales; DDM alters growth with a late-time, redshift-dependent signature. Tomographic shear and \(f\sigma_8(z)\) data provide a route to discrimination.
- **The H₀ tension is independent here.** Neither explanation addresses the recomputed 4.85σ Planck–SH0ES discrepancy.

## 5. Verification & Skeptic's Notes

- **Baryonic suppression:** qualitatively verified across hydrodynamical simulations at \(k\gtrsim1\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}\). Its sufficiency to fully resolve the tension remains contested.
